text: "the M9 frontend redesign together with changes to ticket workflows and assistant behavior" - The release-integrating PR says it integrates M9 and adds release notes; the facts do not establish that all listed workflow and assistant changes are part of this release as described in this release-wide claim.

"beside matching passage titles in the assistant’s Markdown answer" - The citation badges are anchored after a cited passage title in sanitized Markdown when that title appears verbatim. The output’s wording could imply general placement beside a matching passage title, omitting that verbatim-title limitation. Also, this item rephrases the delivered Markdown implementation, not the earlier inline-badge implementation that was deferred.

"Citations can now appear as numbered badges beside matching titles in assistant answers" - This repeats the inline citation feature already described above. The facts support the delivered feature, but the output presents it as a separate feature; the facts describe one implementation, not two distinct badge features.

"unless the assistant has already checked it" - The forced check is skipped if a check has already run in this run; the facts do not say an earlier check by the assistant exempts a later retrieval from the force-once check. The check is guaranteed once after retrieval, not necessarily once per retrieval.

"Version 1.9.0 brings the M9 Frontend Redesign together with the web and assistant changes in this release." - The facts say the release PR integrates M9 and adds release notes, but do not establish that the separately listed assistant changes are all included in v1.9.0.

"unless the ticket match, required information, action, or intent needs clarification" - The prompt policy allows asking before a write for an ambiguous ticket match, missing required information, a hard-to-reverse action with real doubt about intent, or an uncertain route_ticket suggestion. The output’s “action ... needs clarification” is broader than that stated allowance.

"with hover and keyboard-focus previews" - The release fact for [#245] supports a hover/focus tooltip, but separately calls out keyboard-focus behavior only in [#233]. This phrasing is part of the [#245] claim, whose fact says “hover/focus tooltip” rather than specifically describing keyboard focus. However, it is supported by [#233] and therefore not unsupported overall.

"You can count on a rejected change restoring the previous status and showing the error" - The fact says rejected status changes roll back and surface a snackbar carrying the ProblemDetails code; this summary is supported.
"with focus returning to where it was before" - The command palette fact says Esc restores focus to wherever it was before the palette opened. Supported.

"Assistant change confirmations" - This is titled as a confirmation-policy change, but [#223] explicitly says asking before a write remains legitimate only for genuine user decisions and missing information. The item’s following text describes that qualification, so the heading is not an unsupported claim.
"Ticket summary timestamps now use the configured user timezone." - Supported by [#222].

"When semantic evaluation is unavailable or embedding fails, you can still rely on the existing lexical check to provide a verdict." - Supported by [#219], which says the lexical evaluator is the fallback for no Voyage key or embedding failure.

"with hover and keyboard-focus previews" - [#245] supports a hover/focus tooltip, but does not state that keyboard focus is usable to show it. Keyboard-focus support is described in [#233], not in the reintroduced Markdown citation badges described by [#245].

"Inline assistant citations: Citations can now appear as numbered badges beside matching titles in assistant answers" - [#233] says badges are anchored in the streamed answer text by matching citation titles. It does not specify assistant Markdown answers; that behavior is described by [#245]. This repeats and blends the earlier implementation with the later Markdown implementation.

"with previews on hover or keyboard focus" - [#233] supports a CSS-only tooltip on hover or keyboard focus, but the output's separate inline-citation item presents this as the current Markdown answer behavior, which [#233] does not establish.

"The assistant no longer needs to ask again before carrying out a change the user already requested" - [#223] says not to re-ask when the user already requested a change, but explicitly allows confirmation for genuine user decisions, including hard-to-reverse actions with real doubt about intent or uncertain route suggestions. The statement is overbroad as written.

"You can rely on it to ask only when a genuine decision or missing information requires confirmation." - [#223] also permits confirmation for hard-to-reverse actions with real doubt about intent and uncertain route_ticket suggestions; those cases are omitted from the stated rule.

"You can rely on the summary times matching the timezone shown in the ticket details." - [#222] says timestamps are converted to the configured user timezone, matching the detail view. The facts do not establish that the configured timezone necessarily matches the timezone shown in ticket details in every case.

"Add inline citation badges with hover or keyboard-focus previews, retaining the sources list for citations not anchored in the answer." - PR #244 says the #233 inline badge implementation was removed during the Markdown integration, leaving citations in the sources list; inline badges were deferred to #243 and subsequently reintroduced by #245. This entry presents the removed implementation as an addition in the resulting release.

"The assistant could claim a ticket change without a successful tool result or ask you to confirm a change you had already requested." - The live reproduction did not reproduce either reported behavior in five turns; the PR added a missing prompt policy, rather than fixing a behavior observed before this change.

"It now reports a change only after a tool call succeeds and proceeds with requested changes without asking again" - The PR added instructions to the system prompt and verified a live scenario, but says model behavior cannot be guaranteed by the scripted tests. This wording presents the policy as guaranteed behavior.

"so you can rely on those answers being assessed by meaning" - Semantic scoring is used when embeddings are available, but the PR says that path is nondeterministic and falls back to lexical scoring when embeddings are unavailable or fail. The assurance overstates what the change guarantees.

"Add inline citation badges with keyboard-accessible tooltips in assistant answers, retaining a numbered sources list for citations that are not anchored." - PR #233 initially added this, but PR #244 removed its inline-badge implementation during integration and deferred the feature. PR #245 later reintroduced badges over sanitized Markdown. Presenting #233’s implementation as an addition in the final changelog misstates what survived integration.
"The title must be quoted verbatim for a badge to be anchored." - The title must appear verbatim for anchoring, but the facts do not require it to be quoted.

"The assistant no longer asks for confirmation after you have already requested a change, including after correcting an earlier mistake. You can rely on it to report a change only after a tool call succeeds" - PR #223 added these rules to the system prompt and verified a live scenario. It does not establish that the assistant will always follow them; the wording presents model behavior as guaranteed.

"Add inline citation badges anchored to matching titles in assistant answers, with tooltip previews and a sources-list fallback. "**Agent roster in assistant replies:**" - The active roster is injected into the assistant’s system prompt, not necessarily included in its replies.

"**Meaning-based grounding checks:** Grounding checks now compare answer sentences with retrieved passages by meaning, so supported paraphrases and translations can be recognized." - The semantic evaluator scores embedding similarity; the facts report deterministic fake-embedder tests, not live validation that supported paraphrases and translations are recognized in practice.

"Category and Due appear as separate uppercase headers" - The facts say Category was changed to uppercase, but do not say Due was changed; the verification shows Due was already uppercase. The fix separated the headers and uppercased Category.
